Its explanation will be made from imaginary table no. 1.

In the following chart there are four columns. Precautions necessary at the time of measurement

While adopting the first method of measuring national income the following precautions are necessary.

اس طریقے کے تحت، سال بھر میں جتنی بھی معدنی، زرعی، اور صنعتی اشیاء پیدا ہوں یا مختلف لوگ مثلاً ڈاکٹر، وکیل، انجینئر، پروفیسر، کلرک اور مزدور وغیرہ جو خدمات سرانجام دیں، ان سب کی (بازار میں رائج قیمتوں پر) زری مالیت معلوم کر لی جاتی ہے۔ اس کی وضاحت فرضی گوشوارہ نمبر 1 سے ہو جائے گی۔

اگلے نقشے میں چار خانے ہیں پہلے میں مختلف اشیاء درج ہیں جو ملک میں پیدا ہوتی ہیں۔ مثلاً گندم، چینی، کپڑا وغیرہ اور وہ خدمت گار جو یہاں کام کرتے ہیں۔ مثلاً ڈاکٹر، وکیل، مزدور وغیرہ دوسرے خانے میں مذکورہ اشیاء کی پیداوار لکھی گئی ہے۔ تیسرے میں ان کی قیمتیں درج کی گئی ہیں اور آخر میں کل مالیت، اسے معلوم کرنے کا طریقہ یہ ہے کہ فرض کریں گندم کی سالانہ پیداوار تین سو کلوگرام ہے اور قیمت 10 روپے فی کلو ہے۔ لہٰذا گندم کی کل مالیت تین ہزار روپے ہوئی اسی طرح تمام پیدا ہونے والی اشیاء کی کل مالیت درج کر لی جاتی ہے پھر خدمت گاروں کی خدمات کی مالیت بھی اسی میں شامل کی جاتی ہے۔ مثلاً ملک میں کل 5 عدد ڈاکٹر ہیں اور ایک ڈاکٹر کی سالانہ تنخواہ تین لاکھ روپے ہے لہٰذا تمام ڈاکٹروں کی خدمات کی کل مالیت پندرہ لاکھ روپے ہوگی۔ اب آخری خانے کے اعداد و شمار کو جمع کیا جائے تو پتا چلتا ہے کہ ملک میں پیدا ہونے والی تمام اشیاء و خدمات کی پیداوار کی مالیت نوے لاکھ روپے ہے گویا یہ اس ملک کی قومی آمدنی ہے۔

پیمائش کی وقت لازمی احتیاطیں

قومی آمدنی ماپنے کا پہلا طریقہ اختیار کرتے وقت مندرجہ ذیل احتیاطیں لازمی ہیں۔

i۔ دوبارہ شمار ہو جانے سے احتیاط: قومی آمدنی ماپتے وقت ہمیں ایک ہی شے کو دو مرتبہ شمار نہیں کرنا چاہیے کیونکہ بعض اوقات ایسی غلطی ہو جاتی ہے۔ کہ ایک چیز جو مختلف شکلیں اختیار کرتی ہے کئی بار گن لی جائے مثلاً ہو سکتا ہے کہ پہلے تو سال بھر میں پیدا شدہ گندم شمار کی جائے، پھر اس کا آٹا، پھر انہیں سے تیار ہوئی روٹیاں گن لی جائیں۔ تو قومی آمدنی کا اندازہ بالکل غلط ہو جائے گا۔ کیونکہ اس طرح ایک ہی شے یعنی گندم کئی مرتبہ گنی جائے۔ لہٰذا اس غلطی سے پورے طور پر بچنا چاہیے۔

… i.e. how can it be measured? National income can be measured by the following three methods.

1. Sum of the value of production (Product Method)

Under this method, whatever mineral, agricultural and industrial goods are produced in the whole year, or whatever services different people, e.g. doctors, lawyers, engineers, professors, clerks and labourers etc., perform, the money value of all of them (at prices prevailing in the market) is found out. Its explanation will be made from imaginary table no. 1.

In the following chart there are four columns. In the first are entered the different goods produced in the country, e.g. wheat, sugar, cloth etc., and those service-providers who work here, e.g. doctors, lawyers, labourers etc. In the second column the production of the said goods is written. In the third their prices are entered and at the end the total value. The method of finding it is this: suppose the annual production of wheat is three hundred kilograms and the price Rs. 10 per kilo; therefore the total value of wheat became three thousand rupees. In the same way the total value of all goods produced is entered. Then the value of the services of service-providers too is included in it. For example, in the country there are in all 5 doctors and the annual salary of one doctor is three lakh rupees; therefore the total value of the services of all doctors will be fifteen lakh rupees. Now if the figures of the last column are added, it becomes known that the value of the production of all goods and services produced in the country is ninety lakh rupees; as it were, this is the national income of this country.

(Table no. 1) Measurement of national income

Precautions necessary at the time of measurement

While adopting the first method of measuring national income the following precautions are necessary.

i. Precaution against double counting: while measuring national income we should not count one and the same thing twice, because sometimes such an error happens that one thing which takes different forms is counted many times. For example, it may be that first the wheat produced in the whole year is counted, then its flour, then the bread made from it is counted. Then the estimate of national income will become completely wrong, because in this way one and the same thing, i.e. wheat, has been counted several times. Therefore one should fully avoid this error.

paras.text: One way of avoiding this error is that while estimating national income only those things be counted which have taken their final form. The second way of avoiding error is that the value which has been added in the different stages over the original price be counted. This matter will become clear from the following example and table no. 2.
paras.urdu: اس غلطی سے بچنے کا ایک طریقہ یہ ہے کہ قومی آمدنی کا اندازہ کرتے وقت وہ چیزیں شمار کی جائیں جو اپنی آخری شکل اختیار کر چکی ہوں۔ غلطی سے بچنے کا دوسرا طریقہ یہ ہے کہ اصل قیمت میں مختلف مرحلوں پر اس میں جتنی قدر و مالیت کا اضافہ کیا جائے وہ شمار کر لیا جائے یہ بات مندرجہ ذیل مثال اور نقشہ نمبر 2 سے واضح ہو جائے گی۔
paras.pashto: د دې تېروتنې د مخنیوي یوه لاره دا ده چې د ملي عاید د اټکل پر وخت هغه شیان وشمېرل شي چې خپله وروستۍ بڼه یې غوره کړې وي. د تېروتنې د مخنیوي دویمه لاره دا ده چې په اصلي بیه کې په بېلابېلو پړاوونو کې څومره ارزښت زیات شوی، هغه وشمېرل شي. دا خبره به د لاندې بېلګې او نقشې ۲ څخه روښانه شي.

paras.text: ii. Services without remuneration: the second precaution while measuring national income is necessary, that works which are done merely as a hobby, e.g. growing vegetables in the garden of the house, ironing clothes, polishing shoes or getting one’s children to do homework, should not be counted in national income, because these works are in fact not done with the aim of obtaining remuneration.
paras.urdu: ii۔ بلامعاوضہ خدمات: قومی آمدنی ماپتے وقت دوسری احتیاط یہ لازم ہے کہ جو کام محض مشغلہ کے طور پر کئے جائیں، جیسے گھر کے باغیچہ میں سبزیاں اُگا لینا، کپڑے استری کر لینا، جوتا پالش کرنا یا اپنے بچوں کو ہوم ورک کروا دینا اس کام کی مالیت کو آمدنی میں شمار نہیں کرنا چاہیے کیونکہ یہ کام درحقیقت معاوضہ حاصل کرنے کی غرض سے نہیں کئے جاتے۔
paras.pashto: ii. بې‌معاوضې خدمتونه: د ملي عاید د اندازه کولو پر وخت دویم احتیاط دا اړین دی چې هغه کارونه چې یوازې د شوق په توګه کېږي، لکه د کور په باغچه کې سبزي کرل، جامې اوتو کول، بوټان رنګول یا خپلو ماشومانو ته کورنی کار ورکول، د دې کار ارزښت باید په عاید کې ونه شمېرل شي، ځکه دا کارونه په حقیقت کې د معاوضې د ترلاسه کولو په موخه نه کېږي.

paras.text: iii. Goods and services that come into personal use: the third precaution is necessary, that while calculating gross national product all goods and services produced within the country should be counted, but it happens that some part of the production of goods and services remains uncounted, because it is not brought into sale (i.e. to the market for sale), or some things are used by those who produce them themselves. For example, most people live in their own houses, although if they gave these houses on rent to another person they could have income from there in the form of rent; but while calculating gross national product the rents that could potentially be obtained from these houses are not included. One way of avoiding this error is that while estimating national income only those things be counted which have taken their final form. The second way of avoiding error is that the value which has been added in the different stages over the original price be counted. This matter will become clear from the following example and table no. 2.

Table no. 2

ii. Services without remuneration: the second precaution while measuring national income is necessary, that works which are done merely as a hobby, e.g. growing vegetables in the garden of the house, ironing clothes, polishing shoes or getting one’s children to do homework, should not be counted in national income, because these works are in fact not done with the aim of obtaining remuneration.

iii. Goods and services that come into personal use: the third precaution is necessary, that while calculating gross national product all goods and services produced within the country should be counted, but it happens that some part of the production of goods and services remains uncounted, because it is not brought into sale (i.e. to the market for sale), or some things are used by those who produce them themselves. For example, most people live in their own houses, although if they gave these houses on rent to another person they could have income from there in the form of rent; but while calculating gross national product the rents that could potentially be obtained from these houses are not included. In the same way the services provided voluntarily or the services of housewives, and the value of efforts doing one’s own work oneself, are not included, because finding their worth and value is difficult.

iv. Production of the hidden or underground economy: some people do not disclose all the income or production obtained from their land, factory or business, but keep some part of it hidden so that less tax is levied on them. Therefore that part of the value of production or services which is hidden with the intention of saving tax remains uncounted in gross national product. In this, other illegal activities too are included, e.g. income obtained from smuggling, hoarding and black marketing etc. The value of the production of goods and services connected with such activities, whose connection is with the “underground” economy, is about ten per cent of the gross national product that is officially counted.

v. Goods and services produced in the present period: this precaution too is necessary, that while calculating gross national product only those goods and services be included which have been produced in the present period, and the value of the purchase and sale of goods already present should not be counted in it …
